a_priori_proof.argument: RDKit canonical SMILES preserve atomic composition; a molecule graph with zero dummy ('*') atoms cannot canonicalize to a string identical to one produced from a molecule graph containing one or more '*' atoms (different atom-type multiset => different canonical string, always). Given canon_set_star_fraction == 1.0 (every valid PI1M-prefix canonical structure retains its '*' atom(s)) and every in-scope proposal is closed-shell (zero '*' atoms), membership of any in-scope proposal in pi1m_canon is a set-theoretic impossibility independent of chemical content -- novelty_vs_pi1m_prefix_structural = 1.0 is FORCED by representation mismatch, not measured from structural dissimilarity.

does_not_close: Does not attack inscope_validity, inscope_uniqueness, or the SA feasibility gate (separately audited elsewhere, e.g. R-S06).
Does not claim the 12 in-scope proposals ARE non-novel -- only that this instrument cannot possibly determine that either way.
headline: The signed novelty_vs_pi1m_prefix_structural=1.0 result is a structural tautology, not an empirical finding: canon_set_star_fraction=1.0 means every valid PI1M-prefix reference structure retains its dummy-attachment-point atom, so ANY closed-shell candidate -- including 8 closed-shell structures decapped directly FROM the reference corpus itself -- is forced to register 'novel' by pure representation mismatch. The instrument has zero power to return anything but 1.0 for a closed-shell input against this reference population, contradicting the target's own 'lower-bound sanity check' framing (a sanity check that cannot fail checks nothing).

positive_control.evidence: decap_novelty_vs_pi1m_prefix_structural = 1.0 over 8 corpus-derived closed-shell structures (expected <1.0 if the instrument had any power to recognize corpus-native structures; observed all 8/8 flagged 'novel', identical to the in-scope baseline's 12/12)
positive_control.how_planted: For each of the first 8 RDKit-parseable rows in the same 20000-row PI1M prefix the target receipt locks (sha256 fe23c6d1e4b50bd37a231be6b5db50cbc30e71f5252fd4b5c0d91430cf8cee17), replaced every '*' character with '[H]' in the raw SMILES string, re-parsed and canonicalized with RDKit (rdkit 2026.03.2), then ran the target's own verbatim metric_novelty(candidate_canon_set, pi1m_canon).
positive_control.planted_defect: Fed the instrument N=8 closed-shell structures produced by decapping (*  -> [H], i.e. attachment point saturated with hydrogen) real PI1M reference-corpus rows -- structures maximally 'non-novel' by construction, since they are literally derived from members of the reference set itself.

refutation_summary: REFUTES the epistemic content of results.inscope_novelty_vs_pi1m_prefix_structural=1.0 and its accompanying 'novelty_basis_note' characterization as a 'lower-bound sanity check': the metric is a constant function equal to 1.0 for the entire population of possible closed-shell inputs against this reference set, proven both a priori (set-membership impossibility, star_fraction=1.0) and empirically (8/8 corpus-decapped positive-control structures still register 'novel'). Does NOT dispute the target's validity/uniqueness/SA-feasibility findings (untouched, out of scope of this attack), and does NOT dispute that PI1M itself was correctly hash-locked and read; only the interpretability of the signed novelty number is refuted.
